references.text: God's original command to Moses to place the showbread on the table before the Lord's face.
Detailed instructions regarding the showbread: twelve loaves arranged in two rows on the pure table before the Lord.
Description of the table for the showbread and the continual bread that was to be placed upon it.
David receives the holy bread from the priest Ahimelech, illustrating the use of the showbread.
The Levites' responsibility for the showbread, which was to be arranged every Sabbath.
The priests arrange the showbread on the pure table as part of the service in the temple.
Hebrews refers to the holy place with its table and showbread as part of the earthly sanctuary.
Jesus refers to David eating the showbread, linking it to the understanding of the Sabbath and holy bread.
The verse serves as the overarching summary of the entire consecration ceremony, where the placement of the bread is a central example.
Both verses are parts of the same consecration account and emphasize the principle of exact obedience in God's service.
A strong thematic connection between two holy bread symbols (manna and showbread), both placed before God's presence as signs of provision.
